verdict.summary: You create the app with the HubSpot CLI and can connect your own account or a test account within an hour, after ticking an 'unverified app' checkbox. Customers outside your company can install it through OAuth before it is listed: the Marketplace actually requires three active outside installs before it will list you. The listing itself and the optional certification (which needs 60 installs and six months on the Marketplace) are where HubSpot's review comes in.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-3 hours for the app and Composio wiring; several days of extra work for listing materials (verified domain, setup guide). Certification adds a demo video and a security questionnaire.
verdict.approval_wait: None before customers can connect through your install link. HubSpot's findings give no timeline for Marketplace listing review. Certification: HubSpot replies within 10 business days, and the full review should take no more than 60 days after feedback.

gates.name: Developer test account / your own portal
gates.unlocks: You can install your app in your own HubSpot account or a developer test account and complete the OAuth flow through Composio.
limits: You must tick a checkbox to authorize installing an unverified app
Access tokens expire after about 30 minutes (read expires_in), so the app must refresh them

gates.name: Unlisted installs (allowlisted accounts or direct install link)
gates.unlocks: Real customer HubSpot accounts can install the app through the OAuth flow before any Marketplace listing. If you picked 'allowlisted accounts' distribution in the CLI, only the accounts you specify can install.
limits: No numeric install cap was found in the docs
Rate limit of 100 inbound requests per 10 seconds per connected account
Optional scopes are dropped for accounts without that tool, so check what the token actually grants

gates.name: HubSpot Marketplace listing (and optional certification)
gates.unlocks: The app becomes discoverable on the HubSpot Marketplace. Certification later adds the 'certified' badge.
limits: Listing needs at least 3 active installs from unique production accounts outside your organisation
Certification needs at least 60 active unique installs and 6 months on the Marketplace
Only one app can be in certification review at a time
A rejected app can reapply after 6 months
Certification is valid for 2 years and must be renewed
gates.time_to_reach: Listing: once you have at least 3 active outside installs with API activity in the past 30 days. Certification: at least 6 months after listing, with 60 or more active installs; HubSpot replies within 10 business days and the review loop should take no more than 60 days.

steps.title: Create a HubSpot developer account
steps.detail: Sign up for a HubSpot Developer account at developers.hubspot.com/get-started. Your OAuth (public) app must be linked to a developer account. Create a developer test account there as well, so you can test installs.
gotchas: The findings don't confirm whether a paid plan or a particular admin role is needed

steps.title: Create the app project with the HubSpot CLI
steps.detail: Install the HubSpot CLI, authenticate it to your developer account, and run 'hs project create'. When asked, choose Marketplace distribution (or allowlisted accounts if the app is only for specific portals) and OAuth as the auth type.
gotchas: You can no longer create legacy public apps in the old UI, according to a third-party report of 2026 cutoff dates. Use the Projects/CLI flow.
Choose Marketplace distribution if you might ever list the app. Allowlisted distribution limits installs to the accounts you name.
CLI authentication needs your personal access key, so you have to provide it

steps.title: Set redirect URL and scopes in app-hsmeta.json
steps.detail: In the auth block of app-hsmeta.json, add the Composio callback URL as a redirect URL. Declare scopes in requiredScopes, optionalScopes and conditionallyRequiredScopes, with at least the read scope for each CRM object the agent uses. Request only the scopes your agent actually calls, not Composio's full default list.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Marketplace certification rejects scopes the app requests but never uses
Optional scopes are silently dropped for accounts without that tool

steps.title: Upload the project and copy client credentials
steps.detail: Run 'hs project upload'. Then open the project details page in HubSpot, go to the app's Auth tab, and under Client credentials copy the Client ID and Client secret.
gotchas: Keep the Client secret out of source control

steps.title: Point Composio at your own HubSpot app
steps.detail: In Composio, create a HubSpot (toolkit slug 'hubspot') auth config that uses your own credentials instead of managed auth. Paste the Client ID and Client secret, and set the same scopes you declared in app-hsmeta.json.
gotchas: The scopes in Composio must match the scopes declared in the app, or the authorization will request scopes the app doesn't have

steps.title: Run a test authorization in your test account
steps.detail: Start a Composio connection, sign in to your developer test account, tick the checkbox to authorize installing an unverified app, then click Connect app. Check that the connection succeeds and that an API call such as reading contacts works.
gotchas: When something is wrong (for example a bad client_id), HubSpot shows the error on its own OAuth page instead of returning an error to your redirect URL. Read the page if the flow stalls.

steps.title: Make token refresh and throttling production-safe
steps.detail: Refresh access tokens using the expires_in value (about 30 minutes) rather than a hardcoded time. Keep each installation's refresh token, which stays valid until the user uninstalls the app or you revoke it. Throttle to 100 requests per 10 seconds per connected account.
gotchas: Review often flags 401s from missed token refreshes and 429s from missing throttling. Certification needs an API success rate of at least 95%.

steps.title: Onboard your first outside customers
steps.detail: Have customer HubSpot accounts connect through your agent's Composio flow. They will see the unverified-app confirmation. Make sure each one produces real OAuth-authenticated API calls, because installs alone don't count toward the Marketplace threshold.
gotchas: Only unique production accounts outside your organisation, with activity in the past 30 days, count as active installs

steps.title: Prepare listing prerequisites
steps.detail: Link the app to a verified domain and accept the partner agreement if it is required. Publish a public setup guide covering install with screenshots of the scope approval screen, plus configuration, use, disconnection and uninstall. An agent can draft the setup guide text.
gotchas: The Technology Partner Program Agreement requirement comes from a third-party checklist only
Support docs must be publicly reachable

steps.title: Submit the Marketplace listing
steps.detail: Once you have at least 3 active outside installs, submit the app's Marketplace listing from your developer account. There is no fee and no revenue share.
gotchas: The findings don't document how long listing review takes

steps.title: Wait for listing review
steps.detail: HubSpot reviews the listing. Customers can keep using direct installs while you wait.

steps.title: (Optional) Apply for certification
steps.detail: After 6 months on the Marketplace with at least 60 active unique installs, apply for certification. You'll need a demo video that shows a user disconnecting the app, the Uninstall App endpoint being called, and the app disappearing from Connected Apps. You'll also need a completed security questionnaire and the OAuth code flow with no copy-pasting of codes or tokens.
gotchas: HubSpot won't review the app without the demo video
Only one app can be in certification review at a time
Classic CRM cards are not allowed

steps.title: Certification review
steps.detail: HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team replies within 10 business days, and the review loop should take no more than 60 days after feedback is shared. Certification lasts 2 years, and HubSpot sends a renewal notice 90 days before it expires.
gotchas: If the app is rejected, you have to wait 6 months to reapply, and HubSpot won't remind you

requirements.detail: Your OAuth app must belong to a developer account.

requirements.item: Project created via HubSpot CLI (developer platform 2025.2/2026.03)
requirements.detail: New apps are created with hs project create and hs project upload.
Use requiredScopes, optionalScopes and conditionallyRequiredScopes, with at least the read scope for each CRM object used.
Access tokens last about 30 minutes (read expires_in). Refresh tokens last until the user uninstalls the app or you revoke them.
You need unique production accounts outside your organisation, each with successful API activity in the past 30 days, before the Marketplace will list you.
A Marketplace-bound app must be linked to a verified domain.

requirements.item: Public setup guide and support docs
requirements.detail: Must cover install (with screenshots of the scope approval screen), configuration, use, disconnection and uninstall.
Listed as a requirement only by a third-party checklist; not verified.

requirements.item: Certification: 60 installs, 6 months listed, demo video, security questionnaire, 95% API success
requirements.detail: Only needed for the certified badge, not for listing or public installs.

scopes.effect: Basic OAuth scope that Composio's defaults include. Keep it.
Each CRM object your app uses needs at least its read scope. Add the matching .write scope only if the agent writes to that object.

scopes.scope: Composio default bundle (e.g. settings.users.write, account-info.security.read, cms.domains.write, accounting, e-commerce)
scopes.effect: Composio's default list is broad. Requesting scopes you don't use leads to rejection at certification, and optional scopes are dropped for accounts without that tool. Cut the list down to what you actually call.
On a Marketplace-bound app you can't turn these on yourself. You have to request them from HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team, which allowlists them for testing before publication.

blockers.symptom: There's no button for creating a legacy public app in the HubSpot UI
blockers.cause: HubSpot has moved app creation to the Projects-based developer platform. A third-party source reports that legacy app creation was turned off in May and June 2026.
blockers.fix: Create the app with the HubSpot CLI (hs project create, then hs project upload).

blockers.symptom: The Marketplace listing is refused for too few installs
blockers.cause: Installs only count if they come from outside accounts with OAuth-authenticated API activity in the past 30 days. Connecting alone doesn't count.
blockers.fix: Get at least 3 outside production accounts making real API calls through the app before you submit.

blockers.symptom: Review feedback mentions a low API success rate, or 401 and 429 errors
blockers.cause: Tokens aren't being refreshed, or requests aren't being throttled.
blockers.fix: Refresh tokens using expires_in, and throttle to 100 requests per 10 seconds per account. Keep the success rate at 95% or higher.

blockers.symptom: The review is rejected over scopes
blockers.cause: The app requests scopes it doesn't use. This often happens when Composio's broad default list is copied as-is.
blockers.fix: Remove unused scopes, and make the ones only some customers need optional or conditional.

blockers.symptom: Certification isn't reviewed, or is rejected
blockers.cause: The demo video is missing, the app uses classic CRM cards, or it relies on copy-pasted tokens.
blockers.fix: Record the required demo video (disconnect, Uninstall endpoint, removal from Connected Apps) and use the OAuth code flow. If rejected, you can reapply after 6 months.

composio.note: Composio's managed HubSpot app is fine for prototyping. Switch to your own HubSpot app when you want customers to see your app name, control your own scopes and rate-limit budget, or list on the Marketplace. Setting up your own app is self-serve and takes under an hour. To use it, create a Composio auth config with your Client ID and Secret from the app's Auth tab, and register the Composio callback URL in app-hsmeta.json. Trim Composio's broad default scope list down to what your agent uses before you scale.

open_questions: The findings don't confirm whether a free developer account is enough, or whether a paid plan or admin role is needed.
No numeric install cap was found for unlisted or unverified apps. Confirm there is none before onboarding many customers.
How long Marketplace listing review takes, and the exact listing submission steps, were not confirmed (the applying-for-certification page failed to load).
Whether PKCE is required on the new developer platform was not checked.
The full list of sensitive and highly sensitive scopes, and how long their approval takes, was not retrieved.
The verified-domain setup process and the security questionnaire contents were not fetched.
The Technology Partner Program Agreement requirement and the 2026 legacy-app cutoff dates come from third-party sources only.
